$comment: Default lens set for lens-review when the caller passes no args.lenses. A private overlay or stack may supply its own lens set through args.lenses. lens-review adds the readable-code and rule-checks lenses itself.
usage: Workflow({name:'lens-review', args:{ diffs: [{ repo: '<absolute repo path>', base: '<ref>' }], requirement: '<the request as the user stated it>', readingGuide: '<the author C3 reading guide>' }}). Pass lenses and guardrails only to override this file. Named workflows are read at session start: after editing a workflow file, reload skills before calling it by name.

lenses.prompt: Lens: reuse. Should this have been built new at all? Grep the whole repo (outside the diff) for an existing implementation of what the diff adds: the same computation, helper, constant, component or script step. A deliberate duplicate needs an equivalence test or a stated reason; otherwise it is a finding. Quote both locations as file:line.

Lens: contract. Find every caller and consumer of each symbol, file, config key, CLI flag, hook payload or output format the diff changes (git grep across the repo, including tests and scripts that parse it). A caller the change breaks or silently changes is a finding: quote the caller as file:line and state the failure scenario.

Lens: tests. Look for fake green: tests that are skipped, run zero times, assert nothing, or would still pass with the change reverted. Run the repo's test command when one exists and quote the runner's count (for example 'N pass / 0 fail' or 'Tests run: N'). A new branch without a failure-side test is a finding. Stub-shaped tests are fake green too: a test that would still pass if the imported functions returned undefined, assertions that are only toBeDefined or toBeTruthy (or their equivalents), call-only assertions (the function was called, nothing about what it returned or changed), an expected value computed by the code under test, and assertions on data the test built itself.

guardrails: Not defects here: sparse code comments (readable-code K5.14 allows none), a missing test-plan section in a PR body, style preferences, and anything the diff does not introduce or change.
